title: Best AI Tools for Airbnb Hosts in 2026
summary: Hospitable, Conduit, Besty, HostBuddy and Hostaway AI CoHost compared for Airbnb hosts, starting with whether you need a PMS at all.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated August 24, 2026.*


For Airbnb hosts, the AI tool you should buy depends on whether you run a property management system. If Airbnb is your only channel and you have no PMS, Hospitable connects straight to your account and covers messaging, reviews, and pricing. If you already run a PMS, your AI sits on top of it, and the shortlist is Conduit, Besty AI, HostBuddy AI, and your PMS's own assistant.


## Do you need a PMS before you buy an AI tool?


This is the question that decides the rest of the list, so answer it first.


Hosts with a handful of listings, all on Airbnb, can connect a tool directly to their Airbnb account and be running the same week. Hosts on Hostaway, Guesty, or Cloudbeds should treat the PMS as the system of record and choose an AI that reads and writes to it, because a tool that only sees the Airbnb thread cannot see the reservation.


An AI connected to Airbnb alone will answer confidently about a booking it cannot actually read, and on a multi-channel portfolio it will end up contradicting the PMS.


## 1. Hospitable, for Airbnb-first hosts without a PMS


Hospitable connects through an official Airbnb integration. Its[Airbnb software page](https://hospitable.com/airbnb-management-software) describes "a direct connection between your listing and the software," and says "90% of your guest communication runs on autopilot" using automated answers across 20+ topics, with AI-suggested replies for anything not covered by a template.


It goes further than messaging in two ways that matter on Airbnb specifically. Reviews can be randomised, customised, and sent on your behalf at a set time, with AI generating personalised 5-star review suggestions. And "Dynamic Pricing is embedded into the calendar," adjusting rates on real-time market conditions rather than in a separate tool.


Hospitable publishes tier names, Essentials (free), Host, Professional, and Mogul, priced per property per month. The page shows a "from" price that resolves against the number of properties you select rather than a flat published figure.


Watch-out: no voice. Calls still go to you. And once you list on Vrbo and Booking.com at volume, a PMS usually becomes the better system of record.


## 2. Conduit, for hosts who want the phone covered too


Conduit runs one AI agent across phone, SMS, WhatsApp, email, and OTA inboxes, connecting through PMS and OTA integrations rather than sitting on Airbnb alone. The[Hostaway listing](https://www.hostaway.com/marketplace/conduit/) describes "Voice AI to answer or make phone calls with your brand's tone of voice" and "Copilot or autopilot for any guest inquiries or outreach."


On numbers, Cash Flow Street, a 35-property manager, runs at 96% automation, up from 80% at launch, and Haven Vacation Rentals runs at 90%. Both are published case studies naming the customer.


Pricing is published: $18 per unit per month for Messaging, $30 for Guest, $36 for Guest + Devices, $48 for Full Suite, plus a flat $899 per month Startup package.


Watch-out: a host with three Airbnb listings and no phone line will not get value from the voice agent, which is most of what distinguishes it. This is built for portfolios.


## 3. Besty AI, for hosts whose problem is empty gap nights


Besty runs autopilot or draft mode with a real-time two-way sync to Hostaway, per its[marketplace listing](https://www.hostaway.com/marketplace/besty-ai/) . Alongside replies it does gap-night and early check-in upselling, guest retargeting, inquiry winback, a direct booking widget, and AI tasks generated from reviews and conversations.


Besty is built around unsold one and two-night holes, so it suits a calendar that keeps producing them.


Text only, and pricing is not published. The marketplace page offers a two-week free trial.


## 4. HostBuddy AI, for hosts who want drafts rather than autopilot


HostBuddy pulls conversational data and listing details directly from your PMS account and notifies you through Slack, text, and email, per its[marketplace listing](https://www.hostaway.com/marketplace/hostbuddy_ai/) . It is the conservative choice, strong on drafting and escalation.


Its listing does not state whether it writes back, so ask in the demo. Text only, pricing not published.


## 5. Your PMS's own assistant


If you are on Hostaway, AI CoHost handles what Hostaway says is "up to 90% of guest communication," and the company states "AI Replies is available to all users upon request. There is no add-on fee."


With no extra line item to justify, this is the cheapest place to start. Measure what it fails to resolve over a month, then decide whether a third-party tool is worth adding.

## What should an Airbnb host test before buying?


1. Send a message from a real guest account, not a demo. Does the reply match your house rules as they are written today?
2. Ask something the templates do not cover. What does the tool do when it does not know?
3. Ask for a discount. Does it hold your pricing, or negotiate on your behalf?
4. Message in a language you do not speak. Read the reply back through translation.
5. Check what happens at 3am when a guest is locked out.


The second test is the revealing one. A tool that guesses will eventually invent a parking space or a pet policy, and on Airbnb that ends up in a public review.


## Watch-outs for Airbnb hosts specifically


An Airbnb review cannot be retracted once it is posted, which changes the cost of an inaccurate reply. Run draft mode until you have read a few hundred of the AI's answers and trust them.


Automation percentages come from different denominators. Hospitable's 90% and Hostaway's "up to 90%" are not measuring the same thing, and neither is directly comparable to a per-customer figure like 96%.


Keep your listing content current wherever the AI reads it. Most bad AI replies are accurate readings of stale house rules rather than model failures.


## FAQ


### What is the best AI tool for Airbnb hosts?


For hosts on Airbnb without a PMS, Hospitable, because it connects directly and covers messaging, reviews, and pricing in one product. For portfolios that also need phone calls answered, Conduit. If your PMS already includes an assistant, test that first since it usually costs nothing extra.


### Does Airbnb have its own AI for hosts?


Airbnb provides host tools and templated messaging within the platform, but the AI guest messaging products in this list are third-party and connect either directly to your Airbnb account or through a PMS. Check Airbnb's current host tooling before adding a vendor, since the platform's own features change each release.


### Can AI answer phone calls for an Airbnb host?


Conduit runs a voice agent that answers and places calls. Hospitable, Besty, HostBuddy, and Hostaway AI CoHost are text only as of August 2026, so phone calls still reach you or voicemail.


### Will using AI on Airbnb get my account flagged?


Automated messaging through an official integration is ordinary practice and these tools connect through approved routes. What creates risk is content rather than automation: replies that push guests off-platform or contradict your listing can generate complaints, so keep the AI inside the same rules you would follow yourself.


### How much do AI tools for Airbnb hosts cost?


Conduit publishes $18 to $48 per unit per month plus a flat $899 per month Startup package. Hospitable publishes tier names with prices set by property count. Besty and HostBuddy do not publish pricing. Hostaway states AI Replies carries no add-on fee.


### Can AI write my Airbnb guest reviews?


Hospitable does, with randomised templates sent on your behalf and AI-generated 5-star review suggestions. Read them before they send for the first month, because a generic review of a guest who caused a problem is worse than no review.
